//regions: bom1 is Mumbai. Requests already ARRIVE at the Mumbai edge, but the
functions were executing in iad1 (Washington DC) - the Vercel default -
while the database sits in ap-south-1, which is also Mumbai. So every
query a page made travelled India -> US -> India and back, measured at
roughly 300ms of avoidable latency on every dynamic request, compounding
on pages that run several queries in sequence.
Set here rather than with Next's preferredRegion export, which is
deprecated in this version of Next and now only accepts auto/global/home
on Vercel - none of which can name Mumbai.
One region, not a list: a list deploys to ALL of them, and a second
region would only move functions further from the one database.
NOTE: setting this here was observed NOT to move the functions - the
header stayed bom1::iad1 across deploys with this key present. For a
Next.js project the region that actually applies is the one in the Vercel
dashboard, under Settings > Functions > Function Region, and it only
takes effect on deployments made AFTER it is changed. Kept here so the
two agree and nobody later sets one without the other.
Finding it is harder than it sounds, so: open the PROJECT settings, not
the team ones, then Functions in the left sidebar. Function Regions is a
collapsed accordion, and the regions inside it are grouped by continent -
also collapsed. Mumbai is invisible until both it and the Asia Pacific
group are opened. The CDN page has a Function Regions panel too, but that
one only reports where functions ran; it changes nothing.
Hobby allows exactly one region, so Washington has to come off in the
same edit or the deployment fails before it builds. And redeploying an
existing build is refused - 'try again from a fresh commit' - so a new
commit is what actually picks the saved setting up.
